item.title: Zombie Monetarism
item.description: Three prominent economists, including a former Federal Reserve governor and adviser to US President Donald Trump, have just endorsed “soft monetarism” as a way to guide the Fed's approach to inflation. But the "quantity theory" of money failed for good reasons, and those reasons have not changed.

item.title: Taiwan Needs a New Deterrence Strategy
item.description: Emboldened by US President Donald Trump’s war in Iran, Chinese leaders have ramped up their gray-zone coercion against Taiwan in recent months. To avert a Chinese invasion, Taiwan must ensure that other democracies cannot function without it by providing them with more than just semiconductors.

item.title: What a Sino-American G2 Would Mean for Asian Security
item.description: The G2 concept that Donald Trump has lately been touting is a highly unstable proposition, which could make the emergence of a unipolar Asia more likely. Fortunately, Japan remains committed to advancing the far more effective “free and open Indo-Pacific” framework, with India as an indispensable partner.

item.title: Tearing Down the Currency Wall
item.description: Most of the world seems to misunderstand why global capital is not financing the developing world’s climate transition. The real problem lies in the structure of price formation, which policymakers can best address by focusing on three key priorities.

item.title: The Case for a Pay-Where-You-Play Tax System
item.description: The global tax system has repeatedly put corporate interests ahead of people and the planet by allowing multinationals to transfer profits to tax havens. If adopted, the proposed UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation would overturn the century-old rules that make this possible.

item.title: The Canary in the AI Coal Mine
item.description: The greatest danger posed by AI is not the technology itself, but the race to deploy it before we know how to control it. The recent Hugging Face breach shows how seemingly minor human errors can be amplified by AI, underscoring the risks of treating safety as an afterthought.

item.title: The Painful Incompetence of the Indian State
item.description: India’s relatively weak state capacity has long hampered its development. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been promising to address the problem since he came to power in 2014, but his government’s emphasis on centralizing power and strengthening executive control has had the opposite effect.

item.title: This Time Could Be Different for Russia Sanctions
item.description: High inflation and interest rates are eating away at the foundations of the Russian economy and sapping its growth. By hitting its most important sectors, and its essential source of foreign hard cash, new US legislation would pile enormous pressure on the Kremlin just when it is urgently needed.

item.title: Africa’s Energy Curse Is a Political Choice
item.description: It is no secret why African countries with large fossil-fuel reserves nonetheless have failed to reduce extreme poverty or provide reliable electricity to all households. Those in power have made a conscious choice to privilege hard-currency export revenues, some of which then finance elite consumption rather than public investment.

item.title: The EU’s Incredible Shrinking Banking Sector
item.description: At the start of the millennium, all five of the largest European banks had a higher market capitalization than the largest US bank. What explains the fact that a quarter-century later, the largest US bank has a higher capitalization than all five top EU banks combined, and how can European policymakers address this dramatic reversal?

item.title: AI Must Enlarge the Economy, Not Divide It
item.description: To unlock AI’s full economic potential, we must steer it toward expansion. That requires replacing incentives that favor capital over labor with those that reward augmentation and investment in human capability.

item.title: Silicon, Not Software, Will Decide the AI Race
item.description: The AI race is no longer just about building better models. As competition shifts from scientific discovery to deployment, success increasingly depends on computing power, advanced semiconductors, physical infrastructure, and markets large enough to justify the enormous investments they require.

item.title: The Limits of Asia’s Two Major Growth Models
item.description: Data from a period in which both China and India pursued deliberate industrial policies show that neither country's development route is accessible to other countries. At best, their experience can alert policymakers to structural limitations and coordination problems that will require their own homegrown solutions.

item.title: The World Needs Compassionate AI
item.description: With AI having become the frontline of an intense global competition for economic and geopolitical power, speed is rewarded, scale is celebrated, and market dominance is prized above all else. Under such conditions, we risk forgetting the most important question: Whom is this intelligence ultimately meant to serve?

item.title: Trump’s New Tariffs Are an Opportunity to Fight Back
item.description: Once again, President Donald Trump is subverting domestic and international law in an effort to seize a larger fraction of global value and supply chains, and harming the US economy in the process. The longer that businesses and other governments avoid standing up to him, the greater the disaster that awaits us all.

item.title: The AI Boom and the Future of Finance
item.description: Amid reports of mass layoffs, large-scale destruction of books, sweeping copyright violations, and severe environmental damage caused by AI data centers, an increasingly popular refrain is that the AI bubble cannot burst soon enough. AI-related companies have gained some $27 trillion in market value since November 2022, but investments have been largely circular and increasingly debt-financed, whereas revenues still highly speculative. But while a collapse would cause enormous economic pain, no one should assume that it would spell the end of the AI-driven transformation currently underway.

item.title: The Big Picture
Explaining China’s Industrial Competitiveness
item.description: External headwinds have not weakened China’s manufacturing competitiveness. That is because the Chinese economy combines an unusually large manufacturing base, deep supply chains, fast engineering feedback loops, and cutthroat domestic competition to create global powerhouses.

item.title: When Politicians Ignore Economic Expertise
item.description: As politicians encroach on areas that require technical knowledge, the risk of costly policy mistakes increases. The failures of Narendra Modi and Donald Trump show that when it comes to economic policymaking, political acumen is no substitute for a deep understanding of incentives, markets, and institutions.

item.title: The Beijing Model Meets the Brussels Effect
item.description: As Europe races to rebuild its industrial base, China is focusing more on influencing international standards and governance frameworks. The two powers are converging because neither can hope to claim a dominant position in the global energy transition by relying wholly on its traditional strengths.
